newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timorese students protest on Dili anniversary.
newsitem.headline: East Timorese students protest on Dili anniversary.

text.p: Students staged a protest in front of the University of East Timor on Tuesday on the fifth anniversary of the killing of at least 50 demonstrators in the capital Dili, residents said.
"Dili is generally safe, but students are protesting in front of the university," one resident told Reuters by telephone from Dili.
"In front of the campus it is very noisy," another resident said.
Second Sergeant Kurniawan of the Dili city police denied there was any demonstration and said the city was calm.
Residents said riot police were in the streets around the campus in central Dili and the demonstration was continuing after 10:00 a.m. (0200 GMT).
The reason for the demonstration was not immediately clear and telephone calls to the university were not answered.

Indonesian troops killed 50 demonstrators in 1991 following a funeral for an anti-Indonesian activist in Dili, according to an official report. Witnesses and human rights groups estimated about 180 people died.
In past years, November 12 has been a focus for protests against Indonesian rule of East Timor some 2,000 km (1,200 miles) east of Jakarta.
Indonesian troops invaded the eastern, former Portuguese, half of Timor island in December 1975 and proclaimed it as its 27th province the following July.
The United Nations has refused to recognise Indonesian sovereignty over the territory, which has posed a recurring problem for Jakarta in its international relations over the past 20 years.
